engine: Compass judge (moat, quality and ORION's seven dimensions; Jev beliefs over described situations) · ORION prioritisation (Borda over RICE, ICE, WSJF, leverage, Eisenhower) · ORION aftermath

criteria.useful: Useful: Jev's impact score is at least 2 of 4 ("noticeably" moves the goal).
criteria.moat: Defensible: Jev's moat score is at least 2 of 4 (leaves something a competitor would need months to rebuild).
criteria.proven: Proven: the repository holds tests for it, or it is validated against published data.
criteria.verdicts: valuable = useful, defensible and proven · useful, easy to copy = useful and proven but not defensible · promising, unproven = useful, no evidence yet · low value = not useful · rejected on evidence = tried and measured worse or unidentified.

note: The scores are a model's judgment of the descriptions and evidence shown here; the verdict is the fixed rule applied to them. The context told the judge that the code is open source and easy to copy.

items.title: Checked against real F-106B flight and trim data
items.detail: Elevon lift and trim from the same lattice, a rounded-leading-edge blend, and a comparison with NASA's published F-106B trim table (absolute) and 27 flight points (shape), scored leave-one-flight-out.

evidence.line: Lift error at NASA's trim point 63% before, 3% after; elevon within 0.469°; held-out weight spread 6% (target 5%).

why.moat: Moat 1.8 of 4, nearest to: "It leaves something a competitor would need months to rebuild, such as our own code, a signed release or a working process".
why.quality: Quality 3.5 of 4, nearest to: "It sets a standard customers and investors would cite as a reason to trust Archymedes".
why.evidence: Lift error at NASA's trim point 63% before, 3% after; elevon within 0.469°; held-out weight spread 6% (target 5%).

items.title: Real aircraft only, each tied to its NASA report
items.detail: F/A-18 HARV, F-16XL-1 and F-106B: every dimension names the NASA table or figure it was read from; planforms are built from those numbers; no invented layouts.

evidence.line: F-106B's published area, chord and aspect ratio are reproduced from its triangle within 0.1%; the F-16XL planform is 5% larger than the published wing area, and says so.

items.detail: Vortex lattice plus the Polhamus suction analogy and a vortex-breakdown limit, with a band beside every estimate measured by leave-one-wing-out on 200 digitized NASA points. Misses are published.

evidence.line: Held-out band coverage 90% on 9 wings; 2 of 4 pre-registered criteria met, the misses shown.

items.title: Lift that lags in pitching motion
items.detail: One state for the share of vortex lift present, relaxing with a time constant of the order reported for delta wings; exact stepping; reduces to the static polar.

evidence.line: Reproduces the published linear frequency response to 3 decimals; the time constant is the reported order of magnitude, not identified for these aircraft.

items.title: HARV rebuilt as a closed solid
items.detail: Monotone cubic curves through traced stations; every component a closed, oriented, welded 2-manifold; mesh checker tested on known and broken meshes.

evidence.line: Fuselage volume converges to the exact section integral; wing planform within 0.5% of the analytic trapezoid; outlines traced to ±0.3 ft, so no more accurate to the aircraft than its sources.
